rfm_tuples.R: 'At December 31, 2023, we were in compliance with all financial covenants under our credit agreements and the agreements governing our senior notes.' (10-K Item 7 — Liquidity) and identical language in Q1'24 10-Q: 'As of March 31, 2024, we were in compliance with all financial covenants under our credit agreements and the agreements governing our senior notes.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify there is no amendment or waiver disclosed in the same filing nor in subsequent 10-Q; Mode B — derive: if covenant compliance is genuine, then (a) there should be no consecutive amendments shortening the headroom, (b) the credit facility should retain or extend maturity rather than shorten, and (c) the senior-note maturity ladder should be intact.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 7 Debt and Credit Facilities + Q1'24 10-Q Note 8) + edgar_fts.query_fulltext for 'amendment' / 'waiver' within SNDR filings cutoff 2024-05-15
rfm_tuples.M_value: Zero covenant amendments disclosed in either FY23 10-K or Q1'24 10-Q. Revolver maturity extended to November 2027 (matures > 3 years post-cutoff). Senior notes laddered 2024-2028 at weighted-avg 3.68% fixed; outstanding balance $185M (FY23) declined to $185M flat (Q1'24) — no acceleration, no refinancing, no new issuance. Receivables purchase agreement $150M matures July 2024 (i.e., within 2 months post-cutoff) — modest refinance/renewal risk but only $60M drawn (10-K) / $70M (Q1'24) against $150M capacity. Combined undrawn credit + receivables capacity $213.2M at YE'23 vs $185M senior notes. No financial-covenant ratio is disclosed in the filings — typical for IG-style negotiated covenants in private placements.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Standard investment-grade-style debt stack. The Receivables Purchase Agreement maturity (July 2024) is the only near-term touch point but the facility is heavily undrawn and refinancing 364-day receivables programs is routine. No distressed-credit pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: '/s/ Deloitte & Touche LLP   Milwaukee, Wisconsin   February 23, 2024   We have served as the Company's auditor since 2002.' (Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm — both Financial-Statement and ICFR opinions, the latter unqualified)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify auditor identity, location, tenure, and that the ICFR opinion is unqualified; Mode B — derive: if a Big-4 auditor of 22-year tenure issues a clean ICFR opinion on a company with -27.9% trailing drawdown, the distress is operational/cyclical rather than accounting-quality.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K pages 40-42 audit reports; self_text grep for 'material weakness'; auditor_change_tracker (8-K Item 4.01 lookback)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deloitte & Touche LLP (Big 4); auditor since 2002 (22-year tenure). Both reports unqualified. Search for 'material weakness' in 10-K narrative returns only the boilerplate audit-procedure phrase ('assessing the risk that a material weakness exists') — no actual ICFR weakness identified. Critical Audit Matters: (1) claims accruals estimation, (2) goodwill valuation of MLS reporting unit prior to segment realignment — both routine for a trucking company. No Item 4.01 (auditor change) 8-K in lookback. No NT 10-K or NT 10-Q in lookback.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Long-tenured Big-4 auditor, clean ICFR, no late filings, no auditor turnover — the strongest possible disclosure-quality baseline. Drawdown is driven by something other than accounting-quality concerns.

rfm_tuples.R: 'For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2022, and 2021, no customer accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated revenues.' (10-K Note 1 — Summary of Significant Accounting Policies) and risk-factor language: 'a significant portion of our operating revenues is generated from a number of major customers, the loss of one or more of which could have a material adverse effect on our business.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify 10% concentration claim is consistent across all three FY periods; Mode B — derive: if no single customer is >10%, then a single-customer loss is bounded; but the risk-factor language hedges with 'a number of major customers' — check whether dedicated-segment customers are individually disclosed by name (would indicate higher informal concentration).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 1, Risk Factors); revenue_concentration (none disclosed at customer level)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 / FY22 / FY21 all carry the identical 'no customer > 10%' statement — consistent across 3 years. No specific customer is named in the 10-K text. Dedicated operations claim disclosure: ~70% of Truckload revenue comes from dedicated contracts but customer identities are aggregated. The Risk Factor 'we generally do not have long-term contractual relationships, rate agreements, or minimum volume guarantees with our customers' (excluding dedicated/intermodal) is consistent with the spot/contract truckload model.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Diversified customer base by the standard 10% test. The risk-factor language is generic-trucking boilerplate, not a distress indicator. No counterparty concentration red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: Enterprise income from operations $296.4M (2023) vs $600.4M (2022) — 'decreased $304.0 million, approximately 51%, in the year ended December 31, 2023 compared to 2022, primarily due to a decrease in net revenue per order in Logistics, revenue per order in Intermodal, and revenue per truck per week in our Truckload network business.' Q1'24 10-Q: Income from operations $28.7M vs $114.6M (-75% YoY); Operating ratio deteriorated from 90.9% (FY22) to 94.6% (FY23) to 97.8% (Q1'24).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify magnitudes of the income decline and operating-ratio deterioration; Mode B — derive: a 51% FY decline followed by a 75% Q1 sequential deterioration means trough is not yet in. Cross-check whether MD&A frames this as cyclical (industry-wide freight downcycle) vs company-specific.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revenue (excl fuel surcharge) -16% YoY in 2023 ($4.81B vs $5.74B). Q1'24 revenue $1.32B vs $1.43B Q1'23 (-7.7%). Free cash flow Q1'24 = -$14.3M vs +$62.2M Q1'23. Adjusted EBITDA Q1'24 $130.7M vs $223.4M Q1'23 (-42%). MD&A attributes decline to 'continued challenges in the freight environment', 'ongoing pricing pressures', 'continued downward pressure on industry demand' — consistent industry-cyclical language. No disclosure of customer churn, share loss, or service-failure cost. Capex maintained ($112M Q1'24 vs $121M Q1'23) — management is not retrenching.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Real and material cyclical earnings compression — operating margin collapsed from 9.1% (FY22) to 5.4% (FY23) to 2.2% (Q1'24). The MD&A framing is honest about the freight downcycle and does not understate the deterioration. This is a 'cyclical-trough' filing not a 'lying-about-distress' filing. Severity reflects the operational pain, not disclosure failure — what we are NOT detecting is fraud, which is what the honesty-alpha framework is built to identify.

rfm_tuples.R: Share Repurchase Program: 'On February 1, 2023, the Company announced ... up to $150.0 million ... over the next three years ... As of December 31, 2023, the Company had $83.8 million remaining available for repurchase.' Q1'24 10-Q: 'As of March 31, 2024, the Company has repurchased $79.2 million of the $150.0 million authorized.' Plus continuing $0.095/share quarterly dividend declared April 2024 for Q2'24.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: capital-return continuation during -27.9% drawdown and -51% YoY operating-income collapse is either (a) management confidence in cyclical recovery, or (b) discipline-failure. Cross-check insider behavior via Form 4 — if insiders are NOT selling while company buys back stock, signal is constructive (alignment); if insiders are selling while buybacks support the price, signal is exit.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Form 4 audit: 81 Form 4 filings parsed, 152 non-derivative transactions. Only 2 open-market sale transactions (tx_code='S') in 16-month lookback: Devgun Shaleen (CITO) 10,000 sh @ $27.00 on 2023-02-01 = $270K; Reich (EVP CAO) 6,000 sh @ $29.64 on 2023-02-06 = $178K. TOTAL INSIDER SELLING = $447,840 across 2 officers over 16 months — de minimis. Both sales occurred BEFORE the major drawdown began. No CEO or CFO sales. Meanwhile company repurchased $79.2M (Q1'24) and $66.2M during 2023; continued $0.095/qtr dividend ($16.5M Q1'24). Buyback intensity declined in Q1'24 to $13M (vs ~$22M/qtr in Q4'23), consistent with conserving cash in weak Q1 but not stopping. Insider buys: zero open-market purchases either — net signal is 'hold, not sell, not buy' from insiders.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strong Mode B finding: aggressive buyback continuation + de minimis insider selling + maintained dividend = no exit pattern. The capital-return mix shifted moderately toward cash preservation in Q1'24 but the Schneider family control (B-shares) and management are clearly holding through the cycle. Inconsistent with the 'lying about distress' / 'cash out before collapse' profile that the framework targets.

Annualize to ~$120M — consistent with the 1.3% revenue contribution claim on a $5.5B base. Auditor's ICFR scoping exclusion is standard first-year practice. No earnout/contingent-consideration controversy disclosed. The pro forma math reconciles. M&M was reported under Truckload Dedicated segment as part of the Oct-31-2023 segment realignment (MLS + VTL-Dedicated + M&M aggregated). No related-party flag.

Mode-B check: no 'M&A masking a deteriorating core' pattern — the Truckload segment results would still show the cyclical decline even ex-M&M because dedicated and network are reported separately enough that the deterioration would not be plausibly hidden by the acquisition.

rfm_tuples.R: Schneider family dual-class control: Class A (voting) is family-held; Class B (public, NYSE-listed) is what trades. Change-of-control covenants in senior notes define 'change of control' to mean 'the Schneider family no longer owns more than [threshold]' (% threshold detail not fully extracted from filing text). 'We may change our dividend policy at any time ... The Board may, in its discretion, determine to cut, cancel, or eliminate our dividend.' Anti-takeover provisions enumerated in 10-K.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: dual-class family control means equity-holder protections are weaker than at a one-share-one-vote IG-trucking peer; conversely, family is incented to preserve dividend and not to dilute. Combined with insider Form 4 silence (C5), this means the equity-side bear thesis cannot rely on a family-led capitulation/sale event.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Risk Factors (lines 90k-95k) + Note 7 Debt change-of-control covenants
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dual-class structure intact; ~92M Class B shares outstanding (per Q1'24 cover page). DEF 14A (filed 2024-03-15) is the proxy for the annual meeting held 2024-04-29 (per 8-K 0001692063-24-000070); shareholder vote outcomes are routine (bylaw amendment around clawback indemnification, standard director slate). No activist 13D/13G filings disclosed. The 'Schneider family no longer owns more than [threshold]' change-of-control language in the senior notes effectively locks in the family-preferred capital structure — a meaningful Mode B finding for the long-tier case but a negative for any 'distress-driven sale' short thesis.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B insight: the family-controlled structure, combined with the absence of insider selling and continued capital return, makes SNDR structurally an unlikely candidate to be 'lying about distress' — there is no public-side capital-raising or insider-exit incentive to deceive.

summary: SNDR is a clean disclosure profile under cyclical pressure — Big-4 auditor (Deloitte) of 22-year tenure, unqualified ICFR, no material weakness, no late filings, zero covenant amendments, IG-style senior notes laddered through 2028, in-compliance language on all credit agreements both in FY23 10-K and Q1'24 10-Q. Operating margin collapsed from 9.1% (FY22) to 5.4% (FY23) to 2.2% (Q1'24), driven by an industry-wide freight downcycle that the MD&A characterizes honestly. Mode B yields the most informative finding: insiders sold only $448K total over the 16-month pre-cutoff window (152 transactions parsed; only 2 open-market sales by mid-level officers, both pre-drawdown), while the company has executed $79M of a $150M buyback authorization and maintained its quarterly dividend. The Schneider-family dual-class control structurally eliminates an insider-exit channel. This is the opposite of the 'lying about distress' profile the framework is built to detect — the company is cyclically impaired but disclosure quality is high.
